verdict: Booking grew revenue 8% to $7.4B on $51.0B of gross bookings, and net income more than doubled to $2.0B — mostly because a year ago a large foreign-currency loss on its euro debt dragged profit down.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $7.4B, or about +7% on a constant-currency basis

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up 131% from $1.10 a year ago — per-share figures reflect the 25-for-1 stock split on April 2, 2026

kpis.label: Gross bookings
kpis.note: Up 9% from a year ago; room nights rose 5% to 325 million

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: Adjusted net income rose 8% to $2.0B and adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $2.6B

segments.name: Merchant revenues
segments.note: Booking collects the traveler's money itself and pays the hotel or airline — up 15% as Booking.com keeps shifting to this model

segments.name: Agency revenues
segments.note: Hotels and other providers pay Booking a commission and collect the traveler's money themselves — down 7% in the shift to merchant

segments.name: Advertising and other revenues
segments.note: Advertising on Booking's sites and OpenTable restaurant revenue — up 8%

opex.name: Marketing expenses
opex.note: Ads and partner marketing to bring in travelers — 4.7% of gross bookings, vs 4.6% a year ago

opex.name: Sales and other expenses
opex.note: Payment processing for merchant bookings and customer-service costs

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay for the company's staff, including $140M of stock-based pay

opex.name: Information technology
opex.note: Cloud, software and generative AI costs

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on buildings, equipment and software

opex.name: Transformation costs
opex.note: Costs of the company's transformation program

takeaways.title: Merchant is now the engine
takeaways.text: Merchant revenue rose 15% to $5.1B as Booking collects more travelers' payments itself, while agency revenue fell 7% to $1.9B — the ongoing shift from agency to merchant at Booking.com.

takeaways.title: Travel demand stayed resilient
takeaways.text: Room nights rose 5% to 325 million and gross bookings rose 9% to $51.0B. Alternative-accommodation room nights at Booking.com rose 4% and connected-trip bookings kept growing.

takeaways.title: A currency swing flattered profit
takeaways.text: A $195M foreign-currency gain on remeasuring euro-denominated debt — versus a $961M loss a year ago — is the main reason GAAP net income jumped 118%, while adjusted net income rose a steadier 8% to $2.0B.

oneTimers: Foreign currency: a $195M gain on the remeasurement of euro-denominated debt and related derivatives, versus a $961M loss in Q2 2025; equity securities lost $25M in the quarter.
Discrete tax items added $79M of tax expense, including a one-time deemed-repatriation item and the tax impact of intercompany asset transfers.
Transformation costs were $30M in the quarter; the company raised the program's expected annual run-rate savings to about $650M, to be realized by the end of 2027.
Stock split: Booking completed a 25-for-1 stock split on April 2, 2026, and all share and per-share figures in the filings are retroactively adjusted.
otherDetail: Net other income was $60M: interest expense of -$300M, interest and dividend income of +$201M, and other income of +$159M. That $159M was a $195M foreign-currency gain on euro-debt remeasurement, less $25M of net losses on equity securities and $11M of other net losses.
footerNote: Booking Holdings reports no cost of revenue — every cost is an operating expense, so gross profit equals revenue.
